 Watch Chelsea vs Tottenham for free as two old rivals go head-to-head in the evening kick-off today in the Premier League. FourFourTwo has all the details on live streams and TV channels, wherever you are in the world.
 Chelsea vs Tottenham: key information 
 Kick-off time: 5:30pm BST / 12:30pm ET / 3:30am AEDT (Sun)
 Free Stream: NBC via YouTube TV (5-day free trial) 
 TV & Streaming: Sky Sports (UK) / Peacock (US) / Stan Sport (AUS)
 Watch from anywhere: Stream from anywhere with ProtonVPN 
 Chelsea continued their positive start to the season under Xabi Alonso with a Pedro Neto brace in the 2-0 win over Everton last weekend.
 They've had a nice seven-day break, with Spurs also coming into this one off the back of a rare win, beating Coventry 3-1 last Monday.
 Read on as FourFourTwo brings you all the information you need to watch Chelsea vs Tottenham online and from anywhere, including for free, in this Saturday-evening Premier League clash.
 Can I watch Chelsea vs Tottenham for free?
 Chelsea vs Tottenham isn't technically available to watch for free, but there is a way that viewers in the US can stream the game at no cost.
 NBC has live coverage in the States and is available on YouTube TV , which currently comes with a 5-day free trial for new customers.
 Outside the US? Use a VPN to access your free Chelsea vs Tottenham stream from anywhere in the world.

 Viewers in the UK can watch Chelsea vs Tottenham live on Sky Sports .
 Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League will have live coverage of the Premier League clash, which kicks-off at 5:30pm BST.

 Watch Chelsea vs Tottenham on Stan Sport 
 Stan Sport is down in price for 2026/27 to AU$29.99. Chelsea vs Spurs is including on the platform as well as every other Premier League and Champions League game.
 View Deal Chelsea vs Tottenham: Preview 
 Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur renew their London rivalry on Saturday evening, with both sides facing a significant test as they look to strengthen their position in the Premier League. Stamford Bridge provides the setting for one of the weekend’s most intriguing fixtures.
 The Blues will be eager to make home advantage count against their neighbours and were good value for their victory on Merseyside last weekend, with Neto grabbing a brace.
 Emiliano Martinez has undergone surgery on a fractured jaw suffered in the win at Everton, and he has now joined Reece James (knee), Jamie Gittens (ankle), Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha (both unspecified) in the treatment room. Malo Gusto (illness) is also a doubt.
 In the absence of Martinez, 21-year-old Mike Penders is set to become Chelsea’s youngest-ever goalkeeper to start a Premier League match, with the 6ft 7in stop-stopper likely to have a three-man defence in front of him in Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill.
 SEE ALSO How to watch Premier League 2026/27: TV Guide, Streams & Fixtures 
 Tottenham had a lovely moment to begin their 3-1 win over newly-promoted Coventry City last week, as James Maddison, starting his first game in over 500 days, netted a sublime opener to really kickstart their season.
 That then followed goals from Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies, as the Lilywhites grabbed a first win of the season to ease some early pressure on gaffer Roberto De Zerbi.
 Rodrigo Bentancur will serve the second of a three-match ban and remains out along with injured quintet Mykhaylo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall (all knee) and Savio (muscle). Destiny Udogie (knee) missed the win over Coventry and a late call is set to be made on his availability for this one.
 Pedro Porro (hamstring), Omar Marmoush, Tosin Adarabioyo (both calf) and Andrew Robertson (unspecified) are also doubts. Former Chelsea midfielder Conor Gallagher will be pushing for a recall and could play alongside Sandro Tonali and Maddison, while Dejan Kulusevski is back after finally overcoming an almost two years lay-off.
 FourFourTwo's prediction 
 Chelsea 1-2 Tottenham 
 We love an upset and think Tottenham edge this one to really get their season going.
